findings.title: Potential AttributeError when organization_context.member is None and broken paginator selection
findings.body: In `OrganizationAuditLogsEndpoint.get`, `organization_context.member` can be `None` (for example, when a non-member with organization access or an API token accesses the endpoint), so evaluating `organization_context.member.has_global_access` will raise an `AttributeError` when `request.user.is_superuser` is `False`. Furthermore, when `optimized_pagination=true` is passed, `self.paginate` is called with `paginator_cls=OptimizedCursorPaginator` and `order_by="-datetime"`, which is incompatible with `AuditLogEntry.datetime` (a `datetime` object): `OptimizedCursorPaginator` uses `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on the attribute and passes raw integer cursor values into the datetime query filter, causing a `TypeError` (`must be real number, not datetime.datetime`) as soon as any results are returned. Finally, these audit log and paginator changes are completely unrelated to the spans buffer PR.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets cause ValueError in Django QuerySet slicing
findings.body: Both `BasePaginator.get_result` (when `cursor.is_prev` is `True` and `cursor.offset < 0`) and `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_result` (when `enable_advanced_features=True` and `cursor.offset < 0`, or when `cursor.is_prev` is `True`) pass a negative `start_offset` to `queryset[start_offset:stop]`. Contrary to the comments, Django's `QuerySet.__getitem__` explicitly forbids negative indexing and raises `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` whenever `start < 0` or `stop < 0`. Any client supplying a cursor string with a negative offset (e.g. `cursor=0:-1:1` on any endpoint using `BasePaginator` or `DateTimePaginator`, or `cursor=0:-1:0` with `OptimizedCursorPaginator`) will trigger an unhandled 500 error.

findings.title: Evicting excess spans from the Redis ZSET leaves orphaned entries in the redirect hash
findings.body: When `span_count > 1000`, `add-buffer.lua` evicts the oldest spans from `set_key` via `zpopmin(set_key, span_count - 1000)`. However, their span IDs remain registered in the `main_redirect_key` hash (`span-buf:sr:{project_id:trace_id}`). Because `done_flush_segments` in `src/sentry/spans/buffer.py` only deletes `main_redirect_key` entries for spans actually returned from `set_key` during flushing, the redirect entries for evicted spans are never cleaned up on flush and will persist in Redis until the 1-hour TTL (`redis_ttl`) expires, increasing memory usage for large traces and potentially redirecting late child spans to an already-flushed segment.
